Package dev.px.core.registry

Class Registry<T extends Named>

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.registry.Registry<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the registered type
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<T>
Direct Known Subclasses:
CategoryRegistry, CommandRegistry, ModuleRegistry
public class Registry<T extends Named> extends Object implements Iterable<T>
Ordered, name-and-type addressable collection of Named entries.

This exists because the old client had four hand-written copies of the same class — module, element, command, and colour managers each with their own ArrayList, Add(), getByName() and getByClass(). Subclasses now add only the behaviour that is actually specific to them.

Lookups by name are case-insensitive, which is what commands and config files need; lookups by class return the first assignable entry, so asking for a base type gives you the concrete instance registered under it.

    • all

      public List<T> all()
      Returns:
      a live, unmodifiable view of the entries, in order.

      A view, not a copy: it reflects later registrations, and iterating it while registering or unregistering throws. Use clear() to empty the registry, and copy the list first if you must mutate during a walk.

    • clear

      public void clear()
      Removes every entry, notifying onUnregistered(T) for each.

      Exists because the obvious way to write it — iterating all() and unregistering — walks a live view and throws ConcurrentModificationException. Config loads that replace a whole list wholesale need this.
